explanation: In Italy, showing the soles of your feet is considered highly disrespectful because the foot is viewed as a dirty body part, and exposing the sole to someone—especially in a social setting—implies contempt or a wish to bring bad luck. This gesture is deeply rooted in Italian superstition and etiquette, where the foot is associated with negative energy.
local_tip: Always keep your feet flat on the floor or crossed at the ankles, and never point the sole of your shoe toward anyone during conversation or while seated.
regional_note: This rule is consistent across all regions of Italy, though older generations may be particularly sensitive to it.
